Fit the model for one time window

Source: R/fit.R
bruce_fit.Rd

Fit the model for one time window

Usage

bruce_fit(
  d,
  mesh,
  spec = bruce_spec(),
  window = NULL,
  theta_init = NULL,
  fix_theta = FALSE,
  keep_config = FALSE,
  cpo = FALSE,
  drop_stations = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

d

A bruce_data object (usually after bruce_covariates()).

mesh

Mesh from bruce_mesh().

spec

Model specification from bruce_spec().

window

Two dates (first and last day). NULL uses the full range of d$obs. Windows are fitted independently; one month is the tested scale.

theta_init

Optional starting mode for the hyperparameters (on INLA's internal scale, e.g. other_fit$inla$mode$theta from a stable fit with the same structure).

fix_theta

Keep the hyperparameters fixed at theta_init instead of estimating them: INLA then computes a single Gaussian approximation of the latent field, which is much faster. Meant for operational maps with hyperparameters learned from a previous fit, and for fast cross-validation. Hyperparameter uncertainty is not propagated, and theta_init must come from a model with the same structure (same networks with estimated noise, same optional terms).

keep_config

Keep the latent configuration so that posterior samples can be drawn (needed by bruce_predict(n_samples > 0)).

cpo

Compute CPO/PIT.

drop_stations

Station ids excluded from fitting (used by bruce_cv()).

verbose

Passed to INLA.

Value

An object of class bruce_fit.

Details

The linear predictor for an observation of network k at station i, location s and day t is $$\eta = \beta_0 + \delta_k + x(s)^\top\beta + u_i + d_t + w(s, t)$$ where \(\delta_k\) is the network offset (only for bias = TRUE), \(u_i\) the iid station effect, \(d_t\) the city-wide daily AR(1) term and \(w(s,t)\) a Matern SPDE field with AR(1) dependence between days. Each network, and the background, has its own Gaussian likelihood. Background cells share \(\beta_0\), covariates, \(d_t\) and \(w\) but no offset or station effect.

After fitting, the field is checked for collapse (see bruce_spec()); every attempt is recorded in fit$attempts and the outcome in fit$status.

The mesh resolution is also checked against the estimated range: the typical edge of the triangles that contain the data is compared with the posterior mean range (fit$mesh_resolution). When the range is less than five times that edge, a warning is issued: the field is poorly resolved and the range estimate can change with the triangulation (in the Rio de Janeiro application, two meshes of about 1,000 vertices built with the same settings by different fmesher versions gave ranges of 7.7 and 4.1 km).
